findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed a pitcher to be resting in kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC, pitcher was removed. Ensure hand sinks are solely being used for hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the pizza prep cooler to be soiled with food splash. Discussed with PIC, prep cooler will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at frequency that prevents splash accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed utensil holder in drawer left of the pizza oven to be soiled with food debris. 
2) Observed mold on slushee nozzle and front of machine to be soiled. 
3) Observed mold accumulation in and around soda nozzles on soda machine.
Discussed with PIC, ensure non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent accumulation of debris. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed only old copies of the employee health reporting agreement signed. No current copies for the staff. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all staff reads and signs the document. Keep copies in the public health binder. Ensure new hires read and sign the document as a part of onboarding. Inspector will follow-up on 4/10/23.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no valid food handler’s licenses for the facility. CFPM’s available, but not active food handler’s for majority of the staff. Discussed with PIC. Ensure new hires obtain a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment and copies are kept in the facility public health binder. License is valid for 3 years. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

A pair of probe thermometers are observed stored in the wire shelf located above the pizza prep station. One probe is in the corner hole where a rack rod would be and the other is in a small hole on the front face of the shelf. Neither probe has a covering and both are directly contacting the metal of the shelf. Inspector discussed with the PIC and they are aware that the food contact surfaces of the probes should be stored so as to prevent possible contamination. The probes were moved (and cleaned/sanitized) during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

1) Two wiping cloths in the kitchen are observed left out on a counter and a shelf. A new employee is in the process of being trained and a discussion took place in relation to wiping cloth storage between uses. The rags were removed during the inspection to correct. 2) A fresh bucket of sanitizer next to the cash registers is observed soiled. It is believed that the rag was not changed when the bucket was. A discussion tool place with the PIC and they are to ensure that proper training takes place in relation to sanitizer bucket use and preparation. The bucket was remade and a fresh rag supplied to correct.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

The hand sink next to the pizza prep station is observed soiled with what appears to be food debris, as well as having a metal pot stored in it. Hand sinks should be used only for hand washing. The pot was moved and the sink cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Both the top section and the floor of the bottom section of the pizza prep cooler are observed soiled with food debris. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 (A) (C) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.
The top drawer to the right of the pizza preparation station was soiled with debris. This drawer is used to stored cleaned utensils prior to use. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to store cleaned utensils in locations that would not recontaminate them prior to use.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 (C) (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under ¶ (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. 
The second drawer down next tot eh pizza prep station had accumulated debris in it as well as single service lids in opened packages. The PIC was informed of the situation and instructed to maintain single service items in a clean location.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

Observed a box of nacho chips to be stored on the floor in the room used for dry storage. Discussed with the person in charge and directed to maintain foods up off the floor.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
750-280 To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees or provided to consumers who serve themselves.

Observed a cup used for getting flour out of the container below the dough station. Discussed using appropriate scoops (with handles) with the person in charge.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

Observed a box of partially eaten girl scout cookies (tagalongs) stored on top of a container of meats intended for the sandwich prep station. Foods for employee consumption should remain separate from foods intended for consumers. Discussed with the person in charge and the item was moved during the inspection.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination.

Observed packages of plastic containers for nachos to be stored on the floor in the back room. Discussed with the person in charge and directed to ensure that single service items and foods remain off the floor.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. Observed containers in the facility with cooking powders not having labels. Discussed with the manager adding labels to all unlabeled (non-obvious) containers.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Observed cutting boards stored behind/ on top of the faucet for the sink. This posses a possible contamination on clean dishes from the products being cleaned. Discussed with the manager and suggested a different location be found for storage.
